value_json.summary: The assessment is careful, but its conclusion is weaker than the evidence. The supplied code shows a program meant to run on the user's own machine. It reads a local repository folder and saves everything in one local database file that it tries to keep within a 200 MB limit. Its default AI provider is "agent", which means an outside coding agent pulls the work. The web server runs for a long time, with a startup-and-shutdown hook, an optional timer that rechecks the repository, and long-lived MCP connections. MCP is the protocol AI tools use to call AnaxiGraph. The card itself warns against serverless when a long-running process that keeps its own state is required. So the right answer is "no action", not "insufficient evidence". The placements also missed that pulled agent work and a remote-worker file already exist. design.control_model: The controller checks access and eligibility, saves a run, and requests source capture. It then records tasks and assigns bounded worker attempts. Each assignment has an expiry time and an attempt number. Replies advance progress only after validation and a successful saved update. Expired attempts may be replaced within a configured retry limit. Once required tasks succeed, the controller requests publication. A failed required task leaves an explicit failed run with retained accepted work. After restart, the controller resumes from saved state. No separate event service is required.
extension_strategy: Add analysis task kinds with explicit required inputs and returned outputs.

Introduce a separate queue service only if measured task volume exceeds what saved task records can support; keep acceptance decisions in the run record.
design.failure_isolation: A failed worker affects its assigned task while other tasks can finish. A replaced worker's late reply cannot overwrite a newer attempt. A source read failure records its effect before analysis starts; required unreadable input prevents a complete result. A save failure leaves the run awaiting another save attempt and exposes no partial scan as complete. Storage failure prevents accepting new work or advancing progress. Separate worker execution can contain a worker crash, but the supplied evidence does not establish separate processes.
information_flows: Start requests carry repository selection, saved settings, access context, and a caller request identity.
Task assignments carry captured source contents or references to those contents, task identity, attempt number, and settings.
Worker replies carry identified outputs, supporting evidence, uncertainty, or an explicit failure.
Progress reads return the run stage, task outcome counts, last saved update time, and failure details.
Published scans pass to the parent's existing inspection reads under their stable scan identity.
operating_model: Run the controller and completed scan writer inside the existing application. Use the workers already supplying AI analysis.
Use saved task records as the work queue. This avoids a separate queue service but adds task selection and expiry checks to the application.
Resume unfinished runs after restart and replace expired attempts only when retry rules allow it.
Check repeated starts, competing controller attempts, duplicate replies, expired attempts, restart recovery, and interrupted publication.

design.control_model: Each handler checks access and calls one action directly. An analysis action reads inputs, builds findings, and saves a record. The handler then formats the outcome. When returning saved findings, it compares recorded input versions with current versions where access permits. If freshness cannot be checked, it reports that uncertainty. Cancellation reaches the active action and produces an interrupted outcome. No separate scheduling service is proposed.
extension_strategy: Add an analysis action when it needs distinct inputs or work. Reuse access checks, record saving, and result delivery.
Add an interface by translating requests and outcomes while retaining the same action rules.
Make portable record format changes explicit so readers can detect unsupported versions.
Introduce queued work or separate processes only if measured workloads require them; doing so adds recovery and coordination duties.
design.failure_isolation: Each action returns its own outcome, so one failed repository request does not become a successful result or replace an earlier record. Interrupted work is marked incomplete if retained. Setup validates backups and confirmation before restore changes begin. Shared-process failures can still interrupt several requests; this design provides no process-level isolation or crash-resume promise.

Saved records retain the full findings; delivery may shorten them while listing omissions.
Current input checks add a freshness assessment without rewriting the original evidence.

design.control_model: Each request runs once from start to end. The desk passes the request to the pin step. The judge or the edit checker then makes a draft. The limiter checks the draft. Interruption produces no saved record, so earlier records stay in place.
extension_strategy: A new kind of judgment adds a new drafting step that feeds the limiter. Pinning, saving, and labeling stay the same.
New blind-spot rules go in the limiter, so all assessment kinds get them at once.
If findings gain new evidence types, only the pin step and the drafting steps need to read them.
design.failure_isolation: If a scan is missing, the pin step fails and no draft is made. A draft without evidence is turned down by the limiter and is not saved. A failed save leaves earlier assessments unchanged. If s04 cannot report the latest scan, assessments are still shown, labeled unknown. Late replies carry their selection, so they cannot replace a newer browser result. All steps share the parent's process, so a crash there can stop several requests.

design.control_model: A start request reaches the scan owner through the application's access checks. The owner checks eligibility, creates a run, and requests source capture. It saves work assignments and sends them to available workers. Each reply is checked against its saved assignment before acceptance. The owner finishes the run when all assigned work has a recorded outcome. Failed work prevents a complete-success status. No separate progress service or message broker is required.
extension_strategy: Add analysis kinds as new assignment kinds while preserving the same acceptance and evidence rules.
Increase worker concurrency without giving workers ownership of run state.
Split scheduling from result acceptance only if measured workload requires independent capacity; that split would add coordination and recovery work.
design.failure_isolation: A worker failure affects its assignment, while other work may continue. A replacement attempt makes older replies ineligible for acceptance. A capture failure is recorded before dependent work starts. If saving fails, the owner stops accepting results and dispatching new work until saved state can be read safely. After a restart, it resumes from saved assignments and may repeat unfinished work. Losing the shared application or record store can stop every run; separate process protection is not promised.
information_flows: A start request supplies repository selection and saved settings; the application supplies access and eligibility decisions.
Captured source becomes retained analysis input with evidence references and disclosed read gaps.
Worker replies become accepted findings only after their assignment identity and evidence references are checked.
Progress replies identify the run and report phase, known work counts, failures, and whether the total is still unknown.
Saved results reach exploration through the parent's checked read path, with input identity and completion state.
operating_model: Run the owner inside the existing application and use its available workers. Add no separate service solely for scheduling or progress.
Use atomic saved-record updates so accepting a result and marking its work complete cannot disagree.
Permit only one active owner for a run. Reject updates from an owner whose claim has expired or been replaced.
Check duplicate replies, late replies after retry, interrupted saves, and recovery from unfinished assignments.
Check denied starts, unknown eligibility, unreadable files, and source changes during capture.
Verify that saved partial results remain inspectable without appearing complete.

design.state_ownership: The scan owner controls run states, captured input references, assignments, accepted findings, and completion decisions. These records use the application's shared saved-record facilities. Workers hold only temporary assignment data. Source capture retains input bytes through those same facilities. Progress reads report saved counts and the current phase; they do not maintain another counter store. Finalized scans remain unchanged, and a rerun receives a new ID.
design.summary: Give one scan owner control of each run. It checks whether work may start, captures allowed source, assigns analysis work, accepts worker replies, and saves results. Progress comes from the same saved work records.

It suggests letting the scanner name a short list of database operations instead of the concrete AnaxiIndex class. That idea is dependency inversion: shared code describes what it needs, and other code supplies it. Stable Dependencies asks a different question: does code that rarely changes import code that changes often? The payload cannot answer that question. issues.correction: Say that most waits shown for files and processes have limits. Only the brief in-memory locks have none. This supports the conformance score of 77 or slightly higher, not lower.

issues.explanation: The conformance evidence says no lock wait limits are established. But the source shows several waits that do have limits. IndexWriteAuthority.claim uses timeout=0, so it fails at once instead of waiting. compact_closed_index sets busy_timeout=30000, a 30-second SQLite wait. SemanticRefreshCoordinator.close joins threads with a shared deadline. Storage uses _WRITE_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS. Only the short in-memory threading.Lock sections have no limit, and they never wrap slow work.

issues.correction: Add a check that every caller using hold=True releases in a finally block. Treat this as something to verify, not as a confirmed bug.

issues.explanation: RepositoryOperationGate.acquire with hold=True marks work as active. Only a separate release call clears that mark. The supplied code does not show whether callers release in a finally block. If a caller fails and skips release, every later request for that repository and operation gets 'already_running' until the process restarts. This is the 'leaked lock' risk on the pattern card, and the assessment does not list it.

value_json.summary: The assessment is sound, and I approve it. Pessimistic locking means taking exclusive access before changing shared state. The repository already does this in the places where two callers must not claim the same job or the same index file. "Retain" is the right call: nothing in the evidence measures competing writes. The most useful concrete fix the assessment names is real. In api_semantic.py, start records a queued job and then calls thread.start with no error handler. api_scan.py already shows the local fix. The remaining notes are small. Some evidence of bounded waits was missed. The assessment did not mention that the operation gate relies on callers to release it. The confidence score is a little high given the shortened source files.

value_json.summary: The assessment holds up against the supplied source. Several files already give callers one stable entry point and pass the real work to other files: understanding.py, cli.py, storage.py, architecture.py and api.py. The assessment does not ask for one entry file for the whole repository, which is the right call. The two concrete fixes are backed by the source. Two small notes do not change the result: the confidence score is a little high, and this pattern is meant for single files or file groups, not the whole repository.

issues.explanation: The fit score is 82 out of 100. It measures whether Command matches the kind of problem here. That is high, because the automatic detector matched no problem signals and could not count function calls. The rationale holds up, though. Saved jobs that wait, retry, and need an assigned executor are the textbook reason to store an action as data. So the score can stand, but it rests on reading the code, not on the detector.

Scope s04 requires pages to stay tied to the selected scan and query.
A's state ownership gives all lasting data to one saved-record component, and resume creates new attempts.
B's control model continues the same draft after a crash and moves the pointer only when every unit is done.
B's cons say that findings spanning many files need a splitting rule and that cleanup must not overlap with saves.
C's state ownership makes the parent controller the only owner of attempts and completion decisions.
A, B and C list different compatible parents: A lists d734, B lists all three, and C lists 877208.

assessments.change_isolation: A new finding kind needs only new matching rules in the comparison action. A new analysis kind needs a definition of its work units for resume. A new file format version needs an explicit reader. Each of these changes stays inside one action.
assessments.control_flow: The parent's request handler checks access and then calls an action directly. Resume starts a new attempt and asks the parent's analysis action to do the remaining work.
assessments.data_ownership: The saved-record component owns all scans, progress and attempt status. Each action owns only its temporary results. The parent owns access settings and runs the analysis.
assessments.decomposition: The design has one store for saved records and three actions: compare, resume and transfer. Each action decides its own work. The store alone makes lasting changes.
assessments.failure_isolation: Failed comparisons and exports change nothing. An import becomes visible only after it passes checks and a full save succeeds. Each resume gets a new attempt, so old evidence is kept. Everything shares one process, so a process crash is not contained. Recovery uses the last good saved version.
assessments.functional_fit: It covers comparison, resume and transfer. Comparison reads two fixed scans and links each difference to saved evidence. Resume checks that the inputs, settings and analysis version still match before it reuses work. Transfer checks the whole package before saving it. How findings are matched between scans is still undefined.
assessments.justified_complexity: It is low. There are four parts and plain direct calls. The design delays background execution until real workloads need it.
assessments.operating_constraints: It runs inside the parent application. It uses the parent's write limit and the parent's error handling for the CLI and HTTP. Storage accounting is reported as unresolved.
strengths: One component makes every lasting change, so resume and import follow the same failure rules.
A resume always starts a new attempt with a new identifier. Late output from an old run cannot change a newer attempt.
Comparison must report differences in coverage, settings or analysis version. It may not call unmatched findings proven changes.
It needs no queue and no extra service.
weaknesses: Each analysis kind must define reusable work units before resume works for it. The design does not supply these units.
Old attempts and temporary imports are kept, but nothing cleans them up and nothing counts their storage.
Long actions run inside the parent's request call. Closing the connection or cancelling the parent request can stop them.
It works only with parent d734. Its own notes say it may clash with f0c461 and 877208 over who writes saved data and who owns attempts.

assessments.change_isolation: A new analysis kind only defines its input unit and what goes in a piece. A new file format version adds a version number that readers refuse if unknown. A storage rule goes only into the storage counter.
assessments.control_flow: The parent analysis saves each finished unit as a piece and adds it to a draft list. When all units are done, the list is marked complete and the pointer is moved. After a crash, the planner lists the units still missing, and the same draft continues.
assessments.data_ownership: The piece store owns the pieces. The register owns the lists, their states and the pointers. No other part changes them. The parent owns access settings and the analysis that is running.
assessments.decomposition: It splits storage into a store of pieces that are never edited and a register of scan lists and pointers. It adds four helpers: a resume planner, a comparer, a bundle step for export and import, and a storage counter with cleanup. The planner and comparer keep nothing between calls.
assessments.failure_isolation: A crash can leave unused pieces or an open draft, but never a broken finished scan. A pointer conflict leaves the old pointer in place. A damaged piece affects only the units that use it. A failure of the shared disk is still a single point of failure.
assessments.functional_fit: It covers all three actions. Matching fingerprints prove that a piece did not change. Matching fingerprints cannot explain why a piece changed. Matching is per input unit, not per finding, so changes to findings inside a unit still need their own rules.
assessments.justified_complexity: It is higher than A or C. It has six parts, plus fingerprint checks, a moving pointer and cleanup. That cost buys crash safety and cheap comparisons, but only if most findings belong to one unit.
assessments.operating_constraints: It runs inside the application. A pointer may only move if it still holds the expected value, and only parent f0c461 says it can do this. Its tests stop a save at every step and damage bytes in import files.
strengths: A scan becomes complete only after every piece it names is saved, and saved pieces never change. A crash cannot damage a finished scan.
Comparison skips pieces whose fingerprints match, so it only reads pieces that differ.
An imported file can be checked on its own, because each piece carries its own fingerprint.
Storage is counted separately for drafts, finished scans, imported scans and unused pieces. Any future storage-limit rule can use these totals.
It is the only design with a cleanup step for leftovers from failed saves.
weaknesses: A piece covers one input unit, such as one file. Findings that span many files have no rule for which piece holds them.
A resume keeps filling the same draft and has no attempt identifier. The design does not say how output from an older, abandoned run is kept out of the draft.

Each piece's fingerprint covers its findings, evidence and input fingerprint. A change in settings or analysis version changes the fingerprint even when the file did not change. The comparer does not promise to report such setting or version differences.
Resume compares input fingerprints, but the design does not say it checks settings or analysis version before reusing work.
Cleanup must not run while a save is still going on. The fallback rule depends on knowing the age of the oldest open draft.
Many small pieces mean more file operations and more space spent on lists.

assessments.change_isolation: Each analysis kind defines its own work units and the input changes that force a repeat. If an analysis kind cannot do this, it falls back to repeating its unfinished work. Comparison rules and file version readers are added one at a time.
assessments.control_flow: The controller rechecks access and chooses the work that can be reused. It starts workers only for the remaining units and saves each accepted unit with its progress. Comparison and transfer are direct calls. After a restart, unfinished attempts stay incomplete until someone resumes them.
assessments.data_ownership: The controller owns active attempts and decides when work is complete. The store owns scans, units and progress. Transfer owns its temporary import data until the store accepts it.
assessments.decomposition: It has four responsibilities placed inside the parent's existing controller and store: saved work, resume decisions, comparison and transfer. Resume is an addition to the controller, not a separate action.
assessments.failure_isolation: A failed worker keeps the units already accepted. A failed save stops that attempt. A failed import discards only its own temporary data. The controller and the store are still shared points of failure.
assessments.functional_fit: It covers all three actions. Reuse requires that inputs, settings and analysis rules all still match. If reuse cannot be justified, the work is repeated. Comparison must not report missing work in an unfinished scan as a removal.
assessments.justified_complexity: It is low to moderate. It reuses the parent's controller and store and adds no new service. Its extra cost is writing progress records for each unit.
assessments.operating_constraints: It runs inside the parent's application, controller and store. Only one attempt is active per resumed request. Its tests interrupt work just before and just after a unit is saved.
strengths: The parent's controller is the only part that accepts output from workers. Work from a cancelled or older attempt is rejected.
Each finished unit is saved together with its progress record in one step. A crash cannot mark work done before its result is saved.
A newer interpretation gets a new record identity instead of replacing old findings. This helps s04 history views.
It reserves space before it saves new data, and it removes abandoned temporary import data after recovery.
weaknesses: The shared controller and the shared store both remain single points of failure.
How items are matched between scans and which file versions are supported are both still undefined.
The design says to reserve space, but it does not count storage, so the hard storage limit cannot yet be checked.

composition_conflicts: A works only with parent d734 and C works only with parent 877208, so they cannot share one parent as written.
A notes that parent f0c461 wants its own gate to be the only writer, which clashes with A's saved-record component.
B claims to fit all three parents. Parents d734 and 877208 would first need a pointer that moves only when it still holds the expected value.
B's single growing draft clashes with A's new attempt per resume and with C's rule that only the active attempt's output is accepted.
B's cleanup removes pieces that no list names. A keeps earlier attempts and temporary imports, and those rules must agree before both can apply to the same store.
disagreements: B treats equal fingerprints as proof that nothing changed and does not promise to disclose differences in settings or analysis version. A and C both require comparisons to disclose those differences.
B lets a resumed scan keep adding to the same draft. A and C create a new attempt or keep one active attempt, so late output cannot change older work.
A says long operations stay tied to the parent request. C says cancellation keeps saved units and rejects late output. B does not address cancellation.

differences: B stores a scan as pieces named by content fingerprints plus a list of those pieces. A and C store whole saved records with progress units.
B continues the same draft after a crash. A always starts a new attempt. C keeps one active attempt that its controller owns and rejects late output.
Who owns attempts differs. In A the resume action and the saved-record component share this job. In C the parent controller owns it. In B no part tracks attempts.
B alone has cleanup and per-category storage totals. C alone reserves space before writing. A only reports storage as unresolved.
B compares fingerprints for each unit. A and C match findings by their recorded identities and report uncertain matches.
limitations: A and C mostly differ in which parent they fit and which part tracks attempts. Their component lists and failure rules are nearly the same.
All three run inside one process with one shared store. None explores separate processes or separate stores.
Every design keeps transfer as a single checked package. No design offers a different way to move analysis.
unexplored_directions: Signing exported files so that the receiver can tell who made them.
A design that defines matching rules for findings that span many files.
Limits that are checked before any write, with settled rules for what storage counts.
Running long resumes outside the request call, so a dropped connection does not stop them.
Rules for how long old scans, drafts and attempts are kept.

evidence: Scope s03 requires that failures keep valid completed work and leaves storage-limit accounting open.
Scope s04 requires pages to stay tied to the selected scan and query.
A's state ownership gives all lasting data to one saved-record component, and resume creates new attempts.
B's control model continues the same draft after a crash and moves the pointer only when every unit is done.
B's cons say that findings spanning many files need a splitting rule and that cleanup must not overlap with saves.
C's state ownership makes the parent controller the only owner of attempts and completion decisions.
A, B and C list different compatible parents: A lists d734, B lists all three, and C lists 877208.
value_json.summary: All three designs compare saved scans, resume interrupted work and move finished analysis between installations. All three keep finished work safe when something fails. A and C are close to each other. Each has one store for saved records and three actions on top of it. They differ in who tracks attempts: in A the resume action tracks them, and in C the parent's request controller does. B is different. It stores each scan as a list of small pieces, and each piece is named by a fingerprint of its contents. A resumed scan keeps filling the same draft list instead of starting a new attempt. B also adds a cleanup step and counts storage per category. No design settles how storage counts toward the hard limit. No design settles how findings are matched between scans. No design proves who made an imported file.
unknowns: Which saved data counts toward the hard storage limit.
How findings are matched between scans, especially findings that span many files.
Which transfer file versions are supported and how compatibility is decided.
How s04 history views tell newer interpretations and imported scans apart from local ones.
Whether the parents really give the guarantees each design assumes, such as all-or-nothing saves or pointer moves that check the expected value.

value_json.detail: The module wraps persistence-facade operations with repository selection, snapshot resolution, read APIs, and write transactions. Writes acquire SQLite admission with bounded busy retries, apply storage-policy checks around ordinary transactions, and roll back on errors; scan locking serializes scans across processes. Read methods return empty or null results when the requested snapshot or record is unavailable. Graph and ledger queries are delegated to the persistence facade.
evidence: Module imports and facade calls establish SQLite-backed persistence, storage policy use, file locking, and delegated index reads.
Source implementations and docstrings specify transaction handling, repository and snapshot queries, scan run tracking, graph delegation, and finding updates.
